shared_text:
The flight. A regional jet on a passenger flight, arriving at night in visual conditions.

The crew. The captain was the pilot flying and the first officer the pilot monitoring.

What happened. Before the RNAV approach clearance, the crew realised their fuel load meant landing overweight. To avoid this, they descended early, slowed, and extended partial flaps on the approach. After crossing a fix on the approach, they judged more fuel had to be burned and asked for vectors south, off the approach, intending to return to that fix and rejoin it for a more stable approach at this airport at night, which ATC understood. The first officer heard and read back 'turn left heading 220, descend and maintain 10,000 ft'; ATC did not correct it. The captain set 10,000 ft and descended. ATC said to keep that heading until ready to return, and to expect a left turn. The airport was in sight. With enough fuel burned, the first officer requested and received a left turn direct to the fix. Well into the turn, ATC gave a terrain warning and asked if they would climb to 12,000 ft. The crew said they were at 10,000 ft and would climb. ATC, appearing surprised, instructed a climb to 12,000 ft and heading 180, and told them to keep their own terrain clearance. Both pilots believed their clearance was 10,000 ft. The crew climbed at once, confirmed ATC wanted the left turn stopped, and turned right to heading 180.
safe_outcome: Level at 12,000 ft on heading 180, the crew continued towards the airport, asked for a visual approach when close to it, and landed without further incident. There was no conflict with other traffic. No one was hurt and the aircraft was not damaged.
bad_outcome: Another aircraft was crossing nearby. Both crews received TCAS resolution advisories and followed them, and the aircraft passed about 300 feet vertically and half a mile apart. A flight attendant on this aircraft was thrown against a galley cart during the manoeuvre and received a minor injury.
bracket_fill: [climbing / descending / crossing] = crossing; [this aircraft] = this aircraft
notes: Removed under rule 3: both reporters' Cause and Suggestions sections, including their later view that the first officer may have misheard a clearance to 12,000 ft and that the readback was 'missed by all parties', their views on how ATC should check readbacks and turn the aircraft, and the alternatives they listed (holding, a visual approach). Kept from those sections because they are facts or intent at the time: the airport was in sight on the vectors, and the reason for returning to the fix (a more stable approach at this airport at night). Kept: both pilots' belief at the time that they were cleared to 10,000 ft. The report does not establish which altitude ATC actually cleared; the shared text gives what the crew heard, read back and were later told, and does not resolve it. The two narratives are merged: the exchange about climbing to 12,000 ft is from the second, the terrain warning, heading 180 and own terrain clearance from the first. 'To alleviate this threat' is rendered 'To avoid this'. Moved under rule 5: the continued approach, the visual approach and the landing without incident. Removed under rule 6: fix names and runway numbers. Judgement call: 'crossing' fits an aircraft level and turning at 10,000 ft on vectors.
